description: A two-phase framework integrating Cognitive Load Theory and Situated Learning Theory for sequencing technologies in teacher observation training.
title: Scaffolding-Transfer Integration Framework for teacher observational skill development

description: The article frames scale drift as the measurement-stability problem that arises when educational measurement scales must remain interpretable across years and grades.
title: Scale drift across years and grades as a measurement challenge arising from changing instruction, materials, and standards

description: The chapter argues scale is not just a bigger n, drawing on Coburn (2003) and Clarke and Dede (2009).
title: Scaling depth is multidimensional: depth, sustainability, ownership, and evolution beyond participant counts

description: The paper organizes the entire treatment of proportionality around a single way of thinking: two measurable quantities are related proportionally when their measures scale in tandem.
title: Scaling in tandem as the foundational way of thinking for proportional relationships

description: The chapter defines scaling up, building on McDonald et al.
title: Scaling up defined as achieving greater reach with predictable, measurable impact

description: The paper's central construct is the schema-of-the-moment, a momentary functional pattern created by the simultaneous activity of distributed neuronal elements, replacing the structural view of stored mental templates.
title: The schema-of-the-moment: cognition as a transient functional organization of simultaneously active neuronal elements

description: Schema theory, in its broadest sense, is \"a theory of knowledge\" (Rumelhart, 1980) concerning how material is organized, encoded and retrieved from memory.
title: Schema theory as a theory of knowledge: networks of a superordinate concept with supporting information that interface with incoming information

description: The article invokes schema theory and cognitive science to explain how the brain structures knowledge.
title: Schema theory: learning new information depends on relating it to existing mental blueprints

description: Schmidt's claim that second language acquisition requires conscious noticing of features in the input, that learners who notice more learn more, and that noticing the gap between one's own output and the target is a route to change.
title: Schmidt's noticing hypothesis

description: The paper presents Schon's account of tacit knowledge: knowing-in-action (KIA) is knowledge tacit in the way we do things, which 'unconsciously controls how we act in relationship to our environment in any situation'.
title: Schon's knowing-in-action and the distinction between reflection-in-action and reflection-on-action

description: The paper analyzes Schon's account of how master practitioners induct novices into design-like practices.
title: Schon's reflective coaching: learning design-like practice through a dialogue of words and actions

description: The article organizes its inquiry around the idea that the architecture of school choice — the ways school information is presented to parents — systematically shapes parents' knowledge, attitudes, and decisions.
title: School choice architecture as a behavioral design framework

title: School closure as spatial injustice

title: School engagement as the organizing framework for dropout prevention

description: The article frames school entry age as a factor shaping academic growth through second grade, rather than only initial achievement.
title: School entry age as a determinant of early-grade academic growth trajectories

description: The study formulates a segmentation approach that classifies schools into three growth statuses using school-level growth estimates from a three-level hierarchical linear model.
title: Three-segment school growth-status classification based on confidence intervals around school-level growth estimates

title: School social-organizational structure mediates community influences on school safety

title: Science–literacy integration as a partnership for student success

title: Dialectical monism: culture restructures natural mind, and applied research is basic research
